reference: GNU coreutils date (required command: date), using explicit GNU timestamp parsing and POSIX TZ strings. The reference branch runs under system Bash when type -t cannot find the tz builtin; the candidate branch invokes tz. Fixed UTC epochs make the comparisons deterministic.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and documented help metadata
UTC default, negative UNIX timestamps, and UTC/GMT aliases
TZ environment lookup and explicit -z precedence
Built-in US, EU, and Australian daylight-saving transition boundaries
Parsing valid numeric-offset dates with and without seconds
Operator sidecar files through BASHTZ_ZONE_FILE and BASHTZ_ZONE_DIR
Fixed UTC info, parse -V binding, and malformed date rejection.
exclusions: DST-sensitive live now/info comparison needs a fixed clock; fixed UTC info executes as an independent contract.
The suite does not establish historical IANA timezone fidelity, leap seconds, or full malformed-calendar validation.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves tz as a loadable builtin without invoking a timezone operation.
Check help exposes the documented verbs, conversion syntax, and both operator sidecar variables.
cases.script:
help tz > tz-help.txt
help_text=$(< tz-help.txt)
[[ $help_text == *"tz now [-z ZONE] [-V VAR]"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"tz parse 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS] +/-HHMM' [-V VAR]"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"BASHTZ_ZONE_FILE"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"BASHTZ_ZONE_DIR"* ]]
printf 'tz-help-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Compare the UTC default for a pre-epoch timestamp and the explicit Etc/UTC and GMT abbreviations.
cases.script:
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  unset TZ
  tz convert -1
  tz convert 0 -z Etc/UTC
  tz convert 0 -z GMT
else
  TZ=UTC date -d '@-1' "$fmt"
  TZ=Etc/UTC date -d '@0' "$fmt"
  TZ=GMT date -d '@0' "$fmt"
fi

cases.purpose: Compare implicit TZ selection and confirm an explicit -z zone overrides the environment.
cases.script:
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  TZ=Asia/Tokyo tz convert 0
  TZ=Asia/Tokyo tz convert 0 -z UTC
else
  TZ=Asia/Tokyo date -d '@0' "$fmt"
  TZ=UTC date -d '@0' "$fmt"
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the built-in US rule immediately before and at the 2024 spring-forward and fall-back instants.
cases.script:
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
epochs=(1710053999 1710054000 1730613599 1730613600)
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  for ts in "${epochs[@]}"; do tz convert "$ts" -z America/New_York; done
else
  for ts in "${epochs[@]}"; do TZ=America/New_York date -d "@$ts" "$fmt"; done
fi

cases.purpose: Compare parse results for a leap-day timestamp with a positive offset and a pre-epoch timestamp with a negative offset and omitted seconds.
Compare -V assignment with GNU date output while confirming the conversion result is available in the current shell variable.
cases.script:
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  tz convert 1700000000 -z Asia/Tokyo -V rendered
else
  rendered=$(TZ=Asia/Tokyo date -d '@1700000000' "$fmt")
fi
printf '%s\n' "$rendered"

cases.purpose: Compare an operator supplied relative zone file, whitespace/comment parsing, custom names, and its US DST rule with an equivalent POSIX TZ rule.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '# operator-provided rule' 'name = Fixture/Eastern' 'std_off = -18000' 'dst_off = -14400' 'std_abbr = EST' 'dst_abbr = EDT' 'rule = us' > fixture-zone
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
epochs=(1710053999 1710054000 1730613599 1730613600)
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  unset TZ
  export BASHTZ_ZONE_FILE=fixture-zone
  for ts in "${epochs[@]}"; do tz convert "$ts"; done
else
  for ts in "${epochs[@]}"; do TZ='EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2' date -d "@$ts" "$fmt"; done
fi

cases.purpose: Compare a named operator zone loaded through the slash-to-underscore filename rule, including omitted dst_off and fixed-rule defaults.
cases.script:
mkdir -p zones
printf '%s\n' 'name = Fixture/PlusFive30' 'std_off = 19800' 'std_abbr = FCT' 'rule = fixed' > zones/Fixture_PlusFive30
fmt='+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z %z'
if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHTZ_ZONE_DIR=zones tz convert 0 -z Fixture/PlusFive30
else
  TZ='FCT-5:30' date -d '@0' "$fmt"
fi

cases.purpose: Compare tz now and DST-sensitive info against GNU date at a controlled current instant.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a frozen wall clock, or a reviewed clock shim that holds CLOCK_REALTIME constant across the reference and candidate runs. Validate tz now -z America/New_York and tz info Europe/Berlin at fixed UTC instants on both sides of their DST transitions; the current runner provides no clock control, so no operation result is claimed.

cases.purpose: A fixed UTC zone has time-independent offset, abbreviation and rule; exercise info without freezing the clock.
Parse a numeric offset directly into a shell variable, compared with independent GNU date arithmetic.
cases.script: if [[ $(type -t tz) == builtin ]]; then tz parse '2000-01-01 01:00:00 +0100' -V epoch; else epoch=$(date -u -d '2000-01-01 01:00:00 +0100' +%s); fi; printf '%s\n' "$epoch"

cases.purpose: Reject an ordinary malformed date string with the documented usage-error status.
